as_told.title: Harold Malmgren's diary and Richard Bissell briefings on other-world technology

plain: Harold Malmgren, an adviser to presidents Kennedy, Johnson, Nixon and Ford, says Richard Bissell, a senior CIA official whom Michels calls the founder of Area 51, the secret US test site, privately briefed him on "otherworld technologies" the government had been trying to recover and understand, opening with the words "there are things you need to know." Malmgren tells it first-hand and adds that these forces were beyond the CIA's knowledge or control and may have interfered with its work with private industry, while the analyst Matthew Pines, the researcher UAPGerb and Michels repeat it, Michels saying he has seen Malmgren's diary, thinks it genuine, and finds Bissell all over it. The tellers date it variously to 1962, 1963, the 1960s or about 1973, and Michels says it covered past crash retrievals, including a 1933 case he calls Magenta; if true, it would mean the CIA knew of non-human technology decades ago.
